True wind speed, boat speed & heel over the race

Note the light-air parking spell midday July 12 (TWS near 0, speed 2–3kn) and the squall passage around 08:00 July 13 (TWS spike to 39kn, boat speed surge).

Current effect over the race

SOG minus STW (5-min median) — positive means the boat moved over the ground faster than it moved through the water (a favorable push), negative means the reverse. This conflates true water current with leeway and instrument bias, and it's negative in nearly every hour of the race (mean -0.39kn) — more consistent with a systematic leeway/calibration bias than a real, race-wide current signal, so read the moments below as deviations from that baseline, not as raw sign. The worst single hour, Sat 8:00PM CDT (-1.18kn), was in southern Lake Michigan shortly after the start (~42.3–42.5°N, between the start and Saugatuck) — that whole Saturday evening into just after midnight window ran -1.18 to -0.7kn. A second pocket runs Sunday night into Monday (~10pm–midnight and ~4am CDT) around 44.7–45.2°N, between Little Sable and Charlevoix (-0.6 to -0.9kn), and a smaller one Monday ~8–9am CDT approaching the Mackinac Bridge, ~45.5–45.6°N (-0.5 to -0.6kn).

Polar performance (boat speed vs. true wind angle, by wind band)

Every individual 1Hz sample (downsampled to ~19k points), not an averaged line — so gust-driven peaks and the real spread at each angle are visible, not smoothed away. Each dot is colored light→dark by its exact TWS relative to that band's own range (darkest = the windiest moment within that specific band), so a gust stands out clearly against calmer nearby samples — opacity alone washed out once thousands of points overlapped. Dashed: the CM1200's actual VPP-generated rated target speed for that band (representative TWS per band: 5/8/12/16/21kn). Click a band in the legend below to toggle it on/off. Port and starboard are combined onto one side (TWA is direction-agnostic) since mirroring just duplicated the same data. Hover a point for its exact TWA/STW/TWS.

Polar performance, colored by efficiency (actual / target speed)

65% — well below target100% — on target135%+ — above target
Same raw samples and layout as the chart above, but each dot is colored by its own polar efficiency (actual STW ÷ the CM1200's rated target STW for that exact TWA/TWS) instead of by wind speed — so under- and over-performance relative to the boat's own rated polar is visible directly on the plot, not just as a headline average. Red = sailing below the rated target for those conditions, blue = at or above it, gray = on target. Same band toggle and hover behavior as above.

Polar efficiency over time

Actual speed-through-water as a % of the CM1200's ORC-certificate rated speed for that TWA/TWS (5-min median; the raw 1Hz signal is too noisy to read as a line). 100% = sailing exactly at the boat's rated pace for those conditions; below 100% is underperforming it. Race-wide average: 94% beating, 82% reaching, 86% running — reaching is genuinely Photon's weakest point of sail against the rating, not an artifact of an earlier incomplete comparison. Same point-of-sail/TWS shading as above — use it to check whether a dip lines up with light air specifically, or happens across a range of wind strengths within the same point of sail.

Gap to Photon over the race

Positive = ahead of Photon (closer to finish), negative = behind. Thin gray lines are the rest of the Class 4/5 fleet for context (retired boats excluded). Background shading shows Photon's own point of sail at that moment (beating/reaching/running), shaded darker for more wind and lighter for less (hover a band for the exact TWS) — so you can tell light-air running apart from breezy running, not just the point of sail itself. Distance-to-finish is computed ourselves from GPS position plus the official course waypoints (Navy Pier → Turning Mark → Saugatuck → Little Sable → Point Betsie → Charlevoix → Grays Reef → Mackinac Bridge → Finish), not YB Tracking's own dtf field, which we found jumps discontinuously and is unreliable for several boats. Interpolated onto a common 5-min clock; each line stops at that boat's own official finish time, not when its tracker happens to go quiet — a finished boat's distance-to-finish freezes at ~0, so leaving it in would make Photon look like it's "catching up" on a boat that's actually parked at the dock.

Overall fleet rank over time (all ~250 boats, all classes)

Photon's rank by raw distance-to-finish among every boat in the race (own course-based dtf, all classes, boats included once their own start gun has fired; boats that have already finished are ranked ahead by finish order even after their tracker goes quiet, so the field size stays constant instead of artificially shrinking as early finishers drop off the air) — this approximates what the live YB tracker's default position/rank view shows. Background shading is Photon's own point of sail. The steep fall on Sunday July 12 (~110th around noon CDT down to ~132nd by 12:50pm, bottoming near 143rd around 4:50pm) is the light-air parking spell already visible in the wind/speed chart above (TWS down to 4–5kn) — boats already ahead or in different wind kept moving while Photon sat. Ranks in the first couple hours are noisy since not every class/division had started yet (different start guns), so treat only the post-settle trend as meaningful. Photon finished 119th of 233 tracked boats overall by raw elapsed distance — roughly the middle of the fleet, fitting for a mid-rated class.

Where Photon fell behind — and why

Race split into 1-hour windows (on a smoothed gap-to-fleet trend, to avoid noise from sparse tracker pings). For the fleet-median rows, each hour's Δ is the median of every still-racing boat's own gap change over that hour, not the change in the pooled median — the latter breaks whenever boats finish and drop out mid-window, since the remaining pool mechanically skews toward whoever's still racing and can read as a big Photon "gain" that isn't real (a boat parked at the dock, or one that just crossed the line, is excluded from that hour's comparison entirely rather than distorting everyone else's). The tags note how many boats fed each fleet-comparison hour so a delta based on a handful of stragglers late in the race can be read with appropriate skepticism. "Eff." is Photon's actual speed as a % of the CM1200's ORC-certificate rated speed for that TWA/TWS — well below 100% points at boat handling (trim, sail choice, helming). "Sep." is Photon's distance from the fleet's mean position during that hour, and the tags note whether the fleet was covering more ground (SOG) regardless of position. Shown against the fleet median and against three specific rivals — Renegade (Class 4 winner), Black Diamond (Class 4 3rd), and Tango In Blue (sister CM1200) — since averaging across 25 boats of different designs can mask a boat-specific matchup. Monday ~7:20am CDT (a reach at 63% of rated speed) is the standout boat-handling issue — it shows up as a worst hour against every single comparison. Most other worst hours happen at or above rated speed with large positional separation, i.e. routing/course choice rather than speed; the exception is Tango In Blue, a sister ship, where smaller separations mean the SOG gaps are harder to explain by routing alone (e.g. Tango covering 13.3kn vs Photon's 7.8kn at similar positions, Mon ~3:22pm CDT).
Bottom line, fleet-wide: this table's fleet-median delta and Photon's raw polar efficiency are answering different questions, and read together they tell a more complete story than either alone. By delta, 5 of Photon's 6 worst hours against the fleet median are downwind runs in building breeze (10–24kn TWS, Sunday afternoon through Monday afternoon) sailed at or above rated speed but 6–13nm from the fleet's mean position — read as "positional, not speed," but at that separation we can't actually confirm the fleet was sailing in the same wind, so treat that as a hypothesis, not a settled cause (unlike the Black Diamond comparison on the "Light air vs BD" tab, where <0.7nm separation genuinely does support "same conditions"). By raw efficiency, though, Photon sailed well below its polars for real stretches that this delta-based table doesn't surface at all: Sunday 54% average from 8am–12pm CDT (the same light-air window as the Black Diamond catch, bottoming at 39% around Sun 9:00AM CDT) — missed here because the fleet may have been becalmed in the same broad lull, so it didn't show up as *relative* loss even though it was genuinely slow sailing. A second, separate pocket runs Monday 75% average 1–3am CDT, in a real 13–18kn breeze, not calm air — a genuine underperformance this table also doesn't catch. The one hour flagged here as "boat handling" (Monday ~7:20am CDT, 63%) is real but is far from the worst of the race.

Routing divergence (east/west of Photon by latitude)

Longitude offset from Photon's track at the same latitude. Positive = east of Photon, negative = west.

Nearby boats — isolating the location variable

Class 4/5 boats can be scattered across the whole lake, so a class-median comparison mixes routing luck with boat speed. No single boat was near Photon for the whole race except Shmokin Joe (J111, within 5nm for 98% of the race, median 2.1nm) — so instead of one fixed set of companions, the race is split into the distinct sections where a specific boat (any class) was genuinely alongside Photon, each compared using real ORC-style polars, not raw GPS speed.

Gap to Photon vs. nearby boats

"Nearby boats (median)" is the median of the 8 closest currently-racing boats at each moment (membership changes as the fleet spreads out) — same distance-to-finish method as the Class 4/5 gap chart above, just chosen by proximity instead of class. The named lines are each clipped to the specific section where that boat was actually Photon's neighbor (see table below); elsewhere they'd just be showing distance to a boat that was no longer nearby.

Efficiency vs. nearby boats, by race section

For each section, the companion's actual speed is compared to its own real polar (TWA estimated from GPS course-over-ground against Photon's simultaneous wind reading, since we don't have their instruments) — the same efficiency metric used for Photon elsewhere in this report, not raw SOG. "Photon eff." is Photon's own efficiency during that same window, for a fair apples-to-apples read on who sailed relatively closer to their own boat's potential.

Black Diamond averaged 88% over the same window on their own rated polar (Santa Cruz 37, transcribed from their ORC certificate) against GPS-derived speed and Photon's simultaneous TWS/TWD as a stand-in for their own wind reading — reasonable given the two boats were never more than ~0.7nm apart all morning.

VMC = velocity made good on course: rate of closing distance-to-finish, computed identically for both boats from GPS position plus the official course waypoints, so it doesn't depend on Black Diamond's own instruments. Black Diamond out-progressed Photon in every single 30-minute window shown — this was a sustained bleed over 4 hours, not a single lucky puff.

What changed

Not routing: lateral separation between the two boats stayed under 0.7nm the entire window — same track, same rhumb line.

Not maneuvers: Photon logged exactly one tack in this 4-hour window (10:07am CDT, 0.1kn loss) — no tacking/gybing tax.

Not an abnormal polar dip by Photon's own standard: 58% efficiency here is in line with Photon's typical light-air (0–3kn TWS) efficiency all race (43%), not a one-off — but Black Diamond averaged 88% on their own rated polar over the same window, so the two boats' polars weren't equally hard to hit in this air.

What it was: Photon hit two separate near-stalls — STW under 1kn from ~8:45–9:10am CDT (dead run, TWA pinned at 180°) and again ~9:55–10:10am CDT — with the compass heading swinging wildly during both (24°→106°→19°→225°... within minutes), the signature of losing steerage and drifting rather than sailing. Black Diamond's GPS-derived speed dipped too, but only once, for about 10 minutes, and rebuilt to 3kn+ within 15 minutes — noticeably faster than Photon's recovery. Their track also jogged roughly 0.6–0.7nm west of Photon's right through the worst of it, then cut back ahead by 43.83°N — consistent with actively working to find the next puff rather than holding a fixed heading through the hole.
Bottom line: this reads as a light-air/steerage-handling gap in the 0–4kn transition band — keeping the boat moving and finding the next puff — rather than a tactical or routing error. Black Diamond kept pulling away for two more hours as wind built back to 4kn+, so the deficit didn't stop at the hole itself.
